title: Container run profiles
description: Format of registry/run-profiles.json (docs/images-and-ownership.md section 5, SEC-15). A run profile fixes how a container of one image purpose (the `purpose` of registry/image-allowlist.json) is started. status=normative: `docker_run_options` are option groups that every run of the profile contains exactly once, token for token (with the Engine API: the equivalent HostConfig fields listed in the docs); `other_options` are the only other option groups a run may carry; `removal` says when the container is removed. The option set is closed: any other option makes the run non-conforming, and nothing follows the image reference (no command, no arguments). status=to_be_defined: the profile is not defined yet; it needs its own security review, no container of that purpose is run and no image of that purpose is allowlisted until it is defined. A placeholder `{name}` is a whole token and stands for a value matching the pattern of the parameter `name`.

id.description: Equals the image purpose it applies to.

docker_run_options.description: Option groups of `docker run`, each a fixed token sequence. Every run of the profile contains every group exactly once as consecutive tokens, before the image reference.

other_options.description: The only other option groups a run of the profile may carry, each any number of times (name, ownership labels, detached start).

limits.description: Fixed values of the parameters used by docker_run_options. Absent while the values are not fixed; then the client uses provisional constants and no image of this purpose may be allowlisted.

removal.description: always: the container is removed after every run, also after a failure, a timeout and a cancellation, and when a crashed run left it behind.
